draft.title: Egypt's social pyramid
card: Ancient Egyptian society was layered like a pyramid. Few people were at the top and most were at the bottom.
Egyptians saw the pharaoh as a god-king, a living god as well as a ruler. Below came viziers (the pharaoh's chief officials), priests and nobles.
Next came scribes, who could read and write, and craftworkers. Farmers and slaves were at the bottom, and farmers were the largest group.
draft.remember: Few held power at the top. Most people farmed or served at the bottom.

a.q: Who stood at the top of the social pyramid in ancient Egypt?
opts: The pharaoh
The viziers
The priests
The nobles
a.why: The pharaoh ruled over everyone else. Viziers were powerful officials, but they served the pharaoh and ranked below the pharaoh.

b.q: Ahmose lives in Egypt. He reads and writes records for a noble. Which group is he part of?
opts: In the middle, among the scribes
Near the top, among the viziers
At the bottom, among the farmers
At the top, beside the pharaoh
b.why: Scribes could read and write, and they sat below the nobles and above farmers. Viziers were the pharaoh's chief officials, so a man keeping records for a noble is not one of them.
b.clue: Which group was known for reading and writing?

b.best: In the middle, among the scribes
